parts.label: (a)
parts.stem:
An investigation was carried out to measure the rate of photosynthesis at different concentrations of carbon dioxide. Two different plants, barley and sugar cane, were tested at two different temperatures, $10^\circ\text{C}$ and $25^\circ\text{C}$.

The results are shown in Fig. 4.1.

{{figure:figure_4_1.webp}}

Fig. 4.1

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Suggest why, in all four experiments, the rate of photosynthesis became constant as the carbon dioxide concentration increased.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: With reference to Fig. 4.1, describe the difference in the rate of photosynthesis, **at $10^\circ\text{C}$**, between barley and sugar cane.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text:
Sugar cane is a C4 plant. Barley is **not** a C4 plant.

Explain why, **at $25^\circ\text{C}$**, sugar cane had a higher rate of photosynthesis than barley.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Carbon dioxide for photosynthesis enters the leaves through open stomata. Stomata do not stay open all the time.

Changes in environmental conditions can cause stomata to close. Describe these conditions and explain how stomatal closure benefits the plant.
